0|9e45e39dc249c970d99d2681f6bcb55736fd725c|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"ring-buffer: Do not update before stamp when switching sub-buffers
The ring buffer timestamps are synchronized by two timestamp placeholders.
One is the ""before_stamp"" and the other is the ""write_stamp"" (sometimes
referred to as the ""after stamp"" but only in the comments. These two
stamps are key to knowing how to handle nested events coming in with a
lockless system.
When moving across sub-buffers
column2: the before stamp is updated but the write

column1: stamp is not. There's an effort to put back the before stamp to something
that seems logical in case there's nested events. But as the current event
is about to cross sub-buffers
column2: and so will any new nested event that happens

column1: updating the before stamp is useless
column2: and could even introduce new race

column1: conditions.
The first event on a sub-buffer simply uses the sub-buffer's timestamp
and keeps a ""delta"" of zero. The ""before_stamp"" and ""write_stamp"" are not
used in the algorithm in this case. There's no reason to try to fix the
before_stamp when this happens.
As a bonus
column2: it removes a cmpxchg() when crossing sub-buffers!
